To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) we isolated a lymphoblastoid B cell line from a porcine lymphoproliferative disorder, and (ii) we showed that this cell line is capable of producing porcine leukemia virus.
we have isolated and propagated a lymphoblastoid B‐cell line from peripheral blood of a porcine animal that was injected with a cell line producing porcine type C‐retrovirus.
we have developed a new cell line (BI, b and t line) that is histocompatible with miniature swine and produces porcine leukemia virus (PLV).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selection of cell lines of B and T lineage, which produce porcine retroviruses.

the development of a miniature boar model for porcine leukemias and lymphomas, which could be used to study the pathogenesis of these neoplasms and the mechanisms of their control by the immune system.

the development of a miniature boar model of porcine lymphoproliferative syndrome, which could be useful for studying the molecular basis of the disease, for testing new antiviral agents and for the evaluation of the safety of xenografts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BI cell line is of lymphoblastoid nature and that it produces a retrovirus.
the BI cell line and its sublines represent a new histocompatible miniature model for the study of porcine retroviruses and their interactions with lymphocyte populations of b and t cell lineages.
a histocompatible miniature bovine model was selected and that the first step towards a histocompatible porcine model has been achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the porcine retroviruses (PRV) have a wide host range.
the porcine cell line (BI and its sublines) was isolated from a boar that was previously infected with a porcine retroviruses and was suffering from severe non‐neoplatic disease.

we were able to obtain a cell line (BI), which is a transformed lymphoblastoid line, and that we were able, from this line, to obtain sublines which were of B‐ or T‐cell lineages, and were secreting immunoglobulins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a histocompatible miniature boars model allows for the selection of transformed cell lines producing porcine virus.
the BI cell line and its 5 sublines were derived from a boar injected with porcine retroviruses and suffering a non‐neoplasia syndrome.
the use of a histocompatible model is an important step in the study of the pathogenic mechanisms of porcine retroviruses.
